title: In search of a safe zone for sagittal split ramus osteotomy: a cone-beam computed tomography study of the mandibular ramus anatomy
html: Unfavourable split is one of the complications of sagittal split ramus osteotomy (SSRO) and anatomical variation has been attributed as one of the factors. This cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) study aimed to investigate: the ramus thickness; the distance of mandibular lingula (ML) to different ramus landmarks; the horizontal and vertical distance of the ML to the buccal and lingual cortical plates fusion point; and differences between sides of mandible, sex, and ethnicities. This retrospective cross-sectional study consisted of 206 CBCT (412 hemimandibles) of 129 females and 77 males, with a mean age of 33 years.
